newsitem.title: FRANCE: Soccer-Search for goalscorer is Jacquet priority.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Search for goalscorer is Jacquet priority.

text.p: France coach Aime Jacquet's main concern as he tries to build a World Cup-winning team in time for the 1998 finals on home soil is locating a man who can put the ball in the net.
The countdown continues with a home friendly against Turkey on Wednesday and Jacquet concedes his search for a reliable goalscorer may yet lead him back to Manchester United's Eric Cantona.
"I'm completely obsessed by the question of our attack," said Jacquet, after naming his squad for the Turkish game. "There's still this problem of the centre-foward we haven't found."
So why not Cantona, whose international career has been in limbo since he won the last of his 45 international caps against the Netherlands two seasons ago?

"I have sent two very good scouts to see Cantona. Everything is possible," Jacquet said enigmatically, offering at least a glimmer of hope for a player who has already scored 19 goals for his country.
France's Euro 96 performances without Cantona in England in June merely highlighted Jacquet's problems in front of goal.
They played 240 minutes of football in the knock-out stages without scoring, eventually going out on penalties in the semifinals.
Arsenal's new manager Arsene Wenger, the former Monaco coach, has suggested the reason was the loss of AC Milan's Christophe Dugarry to injury, which has continued to play havoc with Jacquet's plans.
He is keen to experiment as much as possible this season and then build the World Cup team in the season leading up to the finals, which start on June 10, 1998.

But Dugarry is still out of action and has yet to make his Milan debut since joining them from Bordeaux. Nicolas Ouedec of Espanyol, who scored in the 2-0 win over Mexico in August, is also unavailable to face Turkey and newcomer Florian Maurice, who made his debut against the Mexicans, has been ruled out for six months.
Jacquet also has to deal with many of his squad playing abroad, although he insists it is not a serious problem.
"I have sent Milan my calendar so they are aware of what's going on," Jacquet said, implying he had done the same with all the clubs concerned.
He also has key players with Internazionale, Parma and Sampdoria in Italy, and Barcelona, Athletic Bilbao and Deportivo La Coruna in Spain.
"I never speak to the players on the phone, only to the trainers to ask if they are available. I know many of the coaches well," said Jacquet, a former French international.

Of far greater concern is whether the striker Jacquet needs will emerge in a French league now deprived of its biggest talents, although Patrice Loko has top-notch support from Ricardo's Brazilian-inspired Paris Saint-Germain midfield.
Abroad his concern is centred on the adaptating process his players are having to go through in an alien environment.
In particular, he is eager to see how playmakers Zinedine Zidane and Youri Djorkaeff respond to life at Juventus and Inter respectively.
"The change of focus they are going through now and the pressure, sometimes excessive there (in Italy), to which they are subjected interest me," Jacquet said.
"We have many things to discuss together which can be useful for the future of the French team."
